title.en: Practice: Syllogisms and statements: what follows and what does not
title.hi: अभ्यास: न्यायवाक्य और कथन: क्या निकलता है और क्या नहीं

section: Practice (written by us, not from a UPSC paper): Syllogisms and statements: what follows and what does not

en.stem: Statements: All pens are books. All books are tables. Conclusions: I. All pens are tables. II. Some tables are pens.
en.why: Pens lie inside books and books inside tables, so all pens are tables. Since pens exist by convention, some tables are pens. Both follow.

en.stem: Statements: Some cats are dogs. All dogs are animals. Conclusions: I. Some cats are animals. II. All animals are dogs.
en.why: The cats that are dogs are inside animals, so I follows. II turns round an all statement; the animal circle can be larger than the dog circle.

en.stem: Statements: No fruit is a stone. Some stones are red. Conclusions: I. Some red things are not fruits. II. No red thing is a fruit.
en.why: The red stones are stones, so they are not fruits: I follows. II goes too far, since other red things could be fruits.

en.stem: Statements: All teachers are readers. Some readers are writers. Conclusions: I. Some teachers are writers. II. Some writers are readers.
en.why: The readers who write may all be outside the teacher circle, so I fails. II is the second statement turned round, which is allowed for some.

en.stem: Statements: Some doctors are singers. Some singers are painters. Conclusions: I. Some doctors are painters. II. No doctor is a painter.
en.why: Two some statements give nothing definite, so neither follows alone. But I and II are a complementary pair: one of them must be true. So either I or II follows.

en.stem: Statements: All roses are flowers. No flower is a tree. Conclusions: I. No rose is a tree. II. Some trees are roses.
en.why: Roses are inside flowers, and flowers and trees do not touch, so no rose is a tree. II contradicts I.

en.stem: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles are polygons. Which of the following must be true?
en.why: All squares are polygons, and squares exist, so some polygons are squares. The first option turns round an all statement; the last two contradict the statements.

en.stem: Statement: The city has banned plastic bags from next month. Conclusions: I. Plastic bags harm the environment. II. Shops in the city may not give out plastic bags from next month.
en.why: II restates what a ban means. I may be the reason, but the statement gives no reason, so it is added from outside.

en.stem: Statements: Only graduates are eligible for the post. Meena is eligible for the post. Conclusions: I. Meena is a graduate. II. All graduates are eligible for the post.
en.why: Only graduates are eligible means every eligible person is a graduate, so I follows. It does not mean every graduate is eligible; there may be other conditions.

en.stem: Statement: A notice reads, "Please use the stairs. The lift is under repair." Assumptions: I. People are able to use the stairs. II. The lift will never work again.
options: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
en.why: Deny I and the request becomes pointless, so I is implicit. A repair suggests the lift will work again, so II is not assumed.

en.stem: Question: Should schools open one hour later in winter? Arguments: I. Yes, children travel in cold and fog, which affects their safety and attendance. II. No, schools have always opened at the same time.
en.why: I gives a real consequence directly related to the question. II only appeals to past practice, which is not a reason.

en.stem: If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match was not cancelled. What can be concluded?
options: It may or may not have rained
The match was played in the rain
en.why: Had it rained, the match would have been cancelled. It was not, so it did not rain.

en.stem: If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match was cancelled. What can be concluded?
options: Nothing certain can be said about rain
en.why: The statement says what rain leads to. It does not say that rain is the only cause of cancellation, so the match may have been cancelled for another reason.

en.stem: Statements: All managers are graduates. Some employees are not graduates. Conclusions: I. Some employees are not managers. II. Some managers are employees.
en.why: The employees who are not graduates cannot be managers, since every manager is a graduate. So I follows. Nothing forces the manager and employee circles to overlap, so II fails.

en.stem: Statement: A shop's records show that it sold more umbrellas in July than in June. Which of the following follows?
options: The shop's umbrella sales in June were lower than in July
It rained every day in July
Every customer bought an umbrella in July
en.why: The first option only restates the statement from the other side. The others give a cause or an extreme claim that the records do not show.
